new_en_desc: Originating in 1330, Germany's oldest city hall features an impressive 61-meter Gothic tower adorned with 130 sculptures of historical figures and a historic corridor.
new_en_tip: 💡 Look out for the wooden face "Platzjabbek" under the clock—it sticks out its tongue at the top of every hour!

new_en_desc: Standing 103 meters tall on the opposite bank in the Deutz district, this skyscraper boasts an open-air rooftop observation deck completely enclosed by safety glass.
new_en_tip: 💡 The golden rule is to enter 45 minutes before sunset, just in time to watch the setting sun bathe Cologne Cathedral in gold and the iron bridge light up.

new_en_desc: Sponsored by Lindt, this interactive museum features a tropical cacao greenhouse, a moving automated production line, and a stunning 3-meter-tall golden chocolate fountain.
new_en_tip: 💡 Head straight to the 3-meter chocolate fountain in the center, where staff hand out free wafers dipped in warm, fresh chocolate!

new_en_desc: Located next to the cathedral, this pinnacle of contemporary art boasts the world's third-largest Picasso collection alongside iconic pop art by Warhol and others.
new_en_tip: 💡 Make your way directly to Room 4 to see Warhol's "Brillo Boxes" and Lichtenstein's "M-Maybe" up close.

new_en_desc: This art museum showcases a magnificent 700-year collection of masterpieces, spanning from the medieval Cologne school to Impressionist and Pointillist works by Monet, Renoir, and Van Gogh.
new_en_tip: 💡 Head to the second floor to admire the dynamic brushstrokes of Impressionism right in front of Monet's "Rough Sea at Étretat."

new_en_desc: Built over the ruins of the ancient Roman city of Colonia, this museum houses an enormous Dionysus mosaic and a remarkable collection of ancient glass.
new_en_tip: 💡 Look through the glass on the first floor to take in the sheer scale of the massive Dionysus Mosaic covering the floor below!

new_en_desc: Founded in 1709, this is the world's oldest fragrance factory and the undisputed birthplace of Eau de Cologne ("Water of Cologne").
new_en_tip: 💡 Join a guided tour (web reservation required) to explore the underground blending room and experience original bergamot scents with a guide in Rococo costume.

new_en_desc: The historic Neo-Gothic flagship store of the world-famous "4711" Eau de Cologne brand.
new_en_tip: 💡 Step up to the "Perfume Fountain" (Parfümbrunnen) at the entrance to lavishly sample real Eau de Cologne welling up from the spring.

new_en_desc: Designed by Peter Zumthor, this architectural masterpiece beautifully envelops the ruins of St. Kolumba Church, which was destroyed during World War II.
new_en_tip: 💡 Visit the vast ruin exhibition room on the first floor to experience Zumthor's serene space, where particles of light stream through holes pierced in the brickwork.

new_en_desc: A true hall of fame for applied crafts, featuring everything from furniture, jewelry, and glass to Bauhaus designs and contemporary products.
new_en_tip: 💡 Don't miss the Bauhaus exhibition corner to admire the product design of Rietveld's iconic "Red and Blue Chair."

new_en_desc: Housed in the former Gestapo headquarters, this center features historical exhibits and a poignant underground prison where the heartbreaking graffiti of former inmates remains on the walls.
new_en_tip: 💡 Descend into the narrow underground cells to witness the scratch marks and foreign-language messages etched into the dark walls by former prisoners.

new_en_desc: One of Europe's premier ethnological museums, dedicated to the cultures, religions, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples from around the globe.
new_en_tip: 💡 Capture a photo of the massive wooden rice barn from Sulawesi, Indonesia, standing in the entrance atrium!

new_en_desc: This museum presents a stunning collection of medieval Christian art, uniquely exhibited within the 11th-century Romanesque St. Cäcilien Church.
new_en_tip: 💡 Quietly admire the wooden crucifixes and intricate ivory carvings displayed within the sacred space of the Romanesque church.

new_en_desc: Located in the Rheinauhafen district, this museum traces the history of sports from the ancient Olympics to Formula 1 cars and pole vaulting equipment.
new_en_tip: 💡 Head to the rooftop terrace to play on the mini soccer and basketball courts overlooking the Rhine River and the city skyline.

new_en_desc: Opened in 1957, this panoramic cable car offers a stunning ride across the Rhine River, with sweeping views of the Cathedral and the lush Rheinpark.
new_en_tip: 💡 Operating only from April to November! Look straight down at the Rhine River from the central gondola and snap a photo with the Cathedral's twin towers in the background.

new_en_desc: Founded in 1860, this historic zoo is famous for its massive 2-hectare Asian Elephant Park and the highly popular baboon rock.
new_en_tip: 💡 Head to the Elephant Park deck at 14:30 daily to catch the Asian elephant herd's bathing and feeding time!

new_en_desc: Adjacent to the zoo, this aquarium features everything from local Rhine River fish to coral reef tropicals, reptiles, and fascinating terrariums.
new_en_tip: 💡 Visit the large underground tank to watch giant manatees and colorful tropical fish gracefully swimming in the coral reef display.

new_en_desc: Spanning 11 hectares, this historic botanical garden features over 10,000 plant species and is crowned by "Flora," a magnificent glass palace built in 1864.
new_en_tip: 💡 Take an elegant photo looking up at the Flora glass palace from the large fountain in the French formal garden!

new_en_desc: Established in 1904 right across from the Cathedral, this iconic historic beer hall is famous for its Kölsch beer, traditionally poured by waiters known as "Köbes."
new_en_tip: 💡 The "Köbes" waiters will automatically bring you fresh, slender glasses of Kölsch—they'll keep pouring until you place your coaster on top of your glass!

new_en_desc: With roots dating back to 1318, this historic tavern serves up traditional cuisine alongside fresh Kölsch poured straight from wooden barrels.
new_en_tip: 💡 Be sure to order the famous local dish "Himmel un Ääd" (Heaven and Earth), a savory mix of blood sausage, mashed potatoes, and stewed apples!

new_en_desc: Immensely popular with the locals on Friesenstraße, this traditional brewery is a premier destination for unfiltered Kölsch served on tap.
new_en_tip: 💡 Enjoy an oversized pork schnitzel alongside fresh Päffgen Kölsch poured directly from traditional wooden barrels!

new_en_desc: Located in the Old Town, this popular and cozy brauhaus is distinguished by its beautiful stained-glass ceiling and homey atmosphere.
new_en_tip: 💡 Grab a seat at a long wooden table beneath the vibrant stained-glass skylight and dig into a crispy roasted pork knuckle (Schweinshaxe)!
